claims.claim: A JavaScript object has properties associating keys with values.
Object literals create objects with listed properties.
Dot and bracket notation access properties, and brackets support a runtime-determined key.
A property name with spaces or a key held in a variable requires bracket notation.
Assigning to a property can add it or replace its value, and an absent ordinary property reads as undefined.
A const binding cannot be reassigned, which is distinct from changing a property on a referenced object.
